chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I said to him, 'A man killed a woman.' He said, 'If the family of the woman intend to kill him, they must pay half his wergild (blood money) and kill him; otherwise, they accept the wergild.'

key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money paid to the victim's family

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money deduction when a man kills a woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'equal retaliation' (qisas) by establishing a financial deduction when a man kills a woman, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the victim's family may either execute the killer after paying half the male wergild or accept the full wergild in lieu of execution. This ruling highlights the flexibility in retribution, allowing the aggrieved party to choose between life for life or financial compensation, a nuance central to Usuli legal theory.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man kills a woman’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the family of the woman intend to kill him, they have to pay half his wergild and kill him, or else accept the wergild (five thousand Dirhams)’.
